name: Jerry Wheeler
bio: Jerry Wheeler was a participant in the San Francisco-to-Moscow Peace Walk who left the march in 1961 to commit civil disobedience at an Air Force base near Tucson, Arizona. He was found guilty and sentenced to six months, held in the Pima County jail.
charges: Civil disobedience / trespass — antinuclear protest at an Air Force base

name: Allan Hoffman
bio: Allan Hoffman was a 19-year-old artist and member of the Committee for Non-Violent Action sentenced to 60 days in the workhouse — then the harshest term ever imposed under the act — for refusing to take shelter during New York's compulsory civil-defense drill on April 28, 1961.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)

name: Elizabeth Just
bio: Elizabeth Just was a 20-year-old New York University student sentenced to 30 days in the Women's House of Detention for defying New York's compulsory civil-defense drill on April 28, 1961 in an antinuclear protest.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: 30 days in the Women's House of Detention

name: Linda Rosenstock
bio: Linda Rosenstock was an 18-year-old arrested in the April 28, 1961 New York civil-defense-drill protest against nuclear-war preparations; she appeared in Adolescent Court and was paroled pending sentencing.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)

name: Ralph Di Gia
bio: Ralph Di Gia was a longtime War Resisters League figure (treasurer of the Civil Defense Protest Committee) arrested at City Hall Park in the April 28, 1961 protest against the compulsory civil-defense drill; as a repeat offender he was held on $500 bail.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: Held on $500 bail for the antinuclear protest

name: M. Tjader-Harris
bio: Mrs. M. Tjader-Harris was a leader of the Civil Defense Protest Committee arrested at City Hall Park in the April 28, 1961 demonstration against New York's compulsory civil-defense drill, a protest against preparations for nuclear war.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: Arrested in the antinuclear civil-defense protest

name: Norval D. Welch
bio: Norval D. Welch, a National Guardian staff member, was among the 42 people arrested at City Hall Plaza in the April 28, 1961 New York civil-defense-drill protest; a first offender, he was taken to night court and paroled.
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill (NY Defense Emergency Act)
sentence: Arrested in the antinuclear civil-defense protest

name: Ted Goertzel
bio: Ted Goertzel was an 18-year-old visiting Antioch College student arrested at Princeton in the April 28, 1961 civil-defense-drill protest when he refused to take cover during the nationwide 'Operation Alert.'
charges: Refusing to take shelter during a civil-defense drill
sentence: Arrested in the antinuclear civil-defense protest

name: Eugene Keyes
bio: Eugene Keyes was a 19-year-old New York University student and Committee for Non-Violent Action pacifist who, in the 1961 'Polaris Action' protest at Groton/New London, Connecticut, swam toward the nuclear submarine Thomas Edison before being seized by Navy frogmen. He was among eight sentenced for the protest.
charges: Interfering with a naval vessel — antinuclear Polaris-submarine protest
sentence: Sentenced with the Polaris Action pacifists

name: Edward Sanders
bio: Edward Sanders was a 21-year-old Harvard student who, in the 1961 Polaris Action at New London, Connecticut, swam toward the nuclear submarine Thomas Edison in protest and was seized by Navy frogmen, among the eight pacifists sentenced.
charges: Interfering with a naval vessel — antinuclear Polaris-submarine protest
sentence: Sentenced with the Polaris Action pacifists

name: Richard Zink
bio: Richard Zink was a 20-year-old Committee for Non-Violent Action pacifist sentenced in the 1961 Polaris Action protests against nuclear-missile submarines at New London, Connecticut; he was ordered to serve 30 days of a six-month term.
charges: Interfering with naval vessels — antinuclear Polaris-submarine protest

name: Ed Guerard
bio: Ed Guerard was a Committee for Non-Violent Action pacifist (a former Marine) who repeatedly swam or paddled toward Polaris submarines at New London, Connecticut and Portsmouth, New Hampshire in 1961 antinuclear protests, and was seized and arrested.
charges: Interfering with naval vessels — antinuclear Polaris-submarine protests
sentence: Sentenced with the Polaris Action pacifists
